questions.stem: A Massachusetts pregabalin prescription was issued five months ago and has already been refilled five times. What is the most defensible next step?

choices.text: Dispense one more refill because the prescription is less than one year old.
Treat the requested refill as a new Schedule VI prescription.
Require new prescriber authorization because the five-refill maximum has been reached.
Dispense the refill because only the six-month limit matters.

questions.stem: Which covered Massachusetts outpatient dispensings belong in the MassPAT submission stream on the basis of the listed drug? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Gabapentin prescribed for postherpetic neuralgia
Pregabalin prescribed for neuropathic pain
Pseudoephedrine sold in an ordinary CMEA retail transaction
None of the listed transactions

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy partially dispenses a methylphenidate prescription at the patient's request. On day 20 after issue, the patient asks a different pharmacy to dispense the remainder. What is the best response?

choices.text: Transfer the balance as a refill because fewer than 30 days have passed.
Decline to dispense the balance there because the remainder belongs to the original pharmacy's partial-fill record.
Wait until day 31, when the remainder automatically becomes a new prescription.
Convert methylphenidate to Schedule III and transfer the balance.

questions.stem: A customer with no pseudoephedrine purchases in the preceding 30 days asks to buy 4.0 grams of pseudoephedrine base today in an ordinary retail transaction. Which specific limit blocks the sale?

choices.text: The 9-gram 30-day limit is exceeded, but the daily limit is not.
The 3.6-gram daily limit is exceeded, but the 30-day limit is not.
Both the daily and 30-day limits are exceeded.
Neither federal retail quantity limit is exceeded.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts prescription for buprenorphine-naloxone is written for opioid use disorder. Which statement best connects the drug's status to the state quantity framework?

choices.text: The naloxone component makes the entire product noncontrolled.
Any opioid-related product is Schedule II and may not have refills.
The product remains Schedule III and may qualify for the Massachusetts 90-day OUD pathway.
The product becomes Schedule VI after its first dispensing.

questions.stem: Place these events in chronological order for a compliant patient-requested Massachusetts Schedule II partial fill when the full remainder is ultimately dispensed.

choices.text: The patient later asks the same pharmacy for some or all of the remainder.
Before the initial dispensing, the patient requests less than the prescribed quantity.
The original pharmacy completes the remainder no later than 30 days after issue.
The original pharmacy makes the initial partial dispensing within five days after issue.

questions.stem: A buprenorphine-naloxone prescription has an unused authorized refill, but the refill is requested more than six months after the prescription's issue date. What controls?

choices.text: The refill cannot be dispensed from that prescription because the six-month issue-date window has passed.
The refill remains valid until six months after the first dispensing.
The naloxone component extends the prescription to one year.
The remaining refill converts into a Schedule VI authorization.

questions.stem: Why should a Massachusetts pharmacist not stop the refill analysis after noticing that 21 CFR 1306.22 expressly addresses Schedules III and IV?

choices.text: Federal law automatically converts every Schedule V drug to Schedule IV at dispensing.
The federal regulation prohibits Massachusetts from regulating Schedule V prescriptions.
Schedule V prescriptions are noncontrolled and have no refill restrictions.
Massachusetts separately applies a five-refill and six-month limit to Schedule V prescriptions.

instruction: Solve each item independently from current official authority before reading anything else in the repository. Record your selected choice IDs and your reasoning, then commit the Phase-1 lock. Do not open data/questions/, data/rules/, the authoring report, the post-lock reveal, the generated site payload, the controller ledger, the plan issue or any git history for these questions before that lock is committed.
content_boundary: Contains only question ID, type, stem and choices plus non-substantive package identity metadata. Excludes keyed answers, explanations, choice analysis, rule and drug identifiers, area, topic, subtopic, difficulty, family, provenance and all author reasoning.
